claim_text: Certain medicines, including renin-angiotensin system inhibitors and potassium-sparing diuretics, can increase serum potassium; additional potassium from supplements or salt substitutes may increase hyperkalemia risk, particularly with impaired renal function.
health_goal_or_outcome: Prevent excess potassium exposure and medication-related hyperkalemia.

population.age_range: Adults; medication and renal context must be individualized.
population.sex_or_life_stage: All; pregnancy requires separate medication review.
population.health_status: People taking medicines that affect potassium or with kidney/heart conditions.
population.other_context: Medication class, dose, kidney function and serum potassium determine risk.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Potassium-containing supplements, electrolyte products and potassium-based salt substitutes.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Potassium Health Professional Fact Sheet describes medication interactions and hyperkalemia risk in susceptible individuals.
limitations: Do not advise stopping prescribed medicines.
Serum potassium and renal function may be needed for clinical decisions.
